claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.

In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, the stage lock only protects an execution once it is actually running: a newer execution can overtake an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping it before it starts.

If a CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued CodePipeline execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment rather than colliding with one already in progress.

Setting the CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue and each one runs in turn, rather than a later commit superseding an earlier one that never got its turn.
AWS CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline type.
When defining a CodePipeline pipeline for `QUEUED` mode, both `executionMode` and `pipelineType` must be set.
The AWS CLI's `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can be used to set `executionMode` and `pipelineType` on a CodePipeline pipeline.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The link to the AWS CodePipeline user guide 'concepts-how-it-works' page documents CodePipeline execution modes.

The Pulumi registry page at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ exists for the `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource, and the resource is described in the section below ('Manage the pipeline with Pulumi').
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment (targeted by a deployment job) that can prevent concurrent runs from reaching the same resource at once.
The Azure Pipelines exclusive lock check is documented at the Microsoft Learn 'approvals' page (learn.microsoft.com/azure/devops/pipelines/process/approvals).
The update-conflicts troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/.
In Azure DevOps, the exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is a stage-level property that controls how the stage referencing an environment with an exclusive lock check behaves.
The default value of the Azure Pipelines stage-level `lockBehavior` is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled/skipped) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, Azure Pipelines runs every queued stage against the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, running them one at a time in order (comparable to `sequential` lock behavior).
`runLatest` is acceptable for a preview environment where only the newest state matters, but not for a stack where every update needs to land.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The registry page /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ exists for the `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts `command: up`, `stack`, and `args` inputs, with `args: --yes` passed to `pulumi up`.
Azure Pipelines deployment jobs use `strategy: runOnce` with a `deploy` lifecycle hook containing steps, and target an `environment`.
When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent runs target the same Pulumi stack, the `pulumi up` of the run that does not get the lease fails with an update conflict error.
The docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists and describes Pulumi update conflicts.
TeamCity's default behavior is to let a build configuration run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
TeamCity has no built-in mechanism, by default, that prevents two builds of the same configuration from racing against the same Pulumi stack.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds', located under the configuration's General Settings.
The default value of TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option is 0, meaning unlimited.

Setting TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option to 1 causes a second build that would otherwise start immediately to be queued behind the first and run only once the first finishes.

Limiting a TeamCity build configuration to one simultaneous build gives the same one-at-a-time behavior as Pulumi Cloud's per-stack update lease, applied earlier so the build never reaches the update conflict.
Pulumi Cloud enforces a per-stack lease that allows only one update to run against a stack at a time.

In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment that a deployment job targets, together with `lockBehavior: sequential` on the stage, serializes deployments so they don't run concurrently.
Azure Pipelines supports an 'exclusive lock' check that can be added to an environment.
Azure Pipelines stages accept a `lockBehavior: sequential` setting.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section 'Serialize deployments with an exclusive lock' (anchor #serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock).
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline pipeline execution mode has a value `QUEUED`.
The default AWS CodePipeline execution mode lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section 'Serialize pipeline executions' (anchor #serialize-pipeline-executions).
In TeamCity, setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 on the build configuration serializes deployments so only one runs at a time.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds'.
The Pulumi TeamCity guide at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section 'Limit concurrent builds' (anchor #limit-concurrent-builds) describing this setting.
